prompt_en: Create a photorealistic wide horizontal ecological field photograph in a rain-cleared temperate rainforest. Old-growth forest structure is the primary subject, reading unmistakably as multi-layer old-growth forest structure. A rain-dark ecological transect makes the complete forest stand the dominant subject: large live trees and smaller cohorts show visibly different trunk diameters and heights; overstory midstory and understory foliage remain separately readable at multiple depths around a broken canopy opening. At least one standing dead snag is structurally distinct from the live trunks, and one or more large fallen logs lie on the forest floor with convincing scale and contact. Wet rot-softened bark, moss mats, and splintered wood fibers retain tactile material detail. An unmistakably adult field observer, guided by the provided appearance reference with general facial continuity and long dark softly waved hair, kneels in practical neutral field clothing and photographs the seedlings beside the foreground nurse log. Gap light and recent rainfall reveal seedlings rooted along the nurse log. Keep the observer small and offset, leaving the snag, log, tree cohorts, and crown layers unobstructed. A diagonal ground-to-crown sightline connects foreground wood, middle trunks, and the opening above. The camera looks diagonally across the gap so foreground log, midground trunks, and high crowns stack without overlap. Cloud-filtered light reveals every height tier without theatrical polish. Use a 24 mm full-frame perspective, deep focus, natural wet surfaces, credible anatomy and contact, suspended mist, natural color, and connected foreground-to-canopy depth.
